<div class="proj-detail-body">
  <div class="proj-detail-prose-wrap">

    <h2 class="proj-detail-h2">About the project</h2>
    <p class="proj-detail-p">Stars slow down over their lifetimes &mdash; much like a spinning top decelerating on a table. Mark Popinchalk's research group at the American Museum of Natural History uses NASA's Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) to measure stellar rotation rates, turning spin into a clock for determining how old a star is. This 2025 SCoPE Seed Grant project, supported through Arizona State University, builds on Popinchalk's completed 2023 work by expanding its reach to entirely new audiences.</p>
    <p class="proj-detail-p">The project creates an educational program guide that demonstrates various cosmic timescales using TESS data in OpenSpace, and plans an active social media campaign with accessible explanations of stellar aging for general audiences. Popinchalk brings direct experience as a former Science Educator at AMNH, co-host of Astronomy on Tap NYC, and regular presenter at the Hayden Planetarium.</p>

    <div class="proj-facts-row">
      <span class="proj-fact">NASA Astrophysics Division</span>
      <span class="proj-fact">TESS satellite data</span>
      <span class="proj-fact">Stellar rotation &amp; gyrochronology</span>
      <span class="proj-fact">Social media outreach</span>
      <span class="proj-fact">Hayden Planetarium</span>
    </div>

    <h2 class="proj-detail-h2">How OpenSpace is used</h2>
    <p class="proj-detail-p">TESS observational data on stellar rotation rates is incorporated directly into OpenSpace, enabling live planetarium presentations that show the relationship between spin and stellar age. The project produces a program guide for educators using this new dataset alongside other cosmic discoveries to illustrate galactic timescales in an interactive setting.</p>
    <p class="proj-detail-p">The 2025 phase specifically focuses on using OpenSpace-based content to reach audiences beyond the planetarium &mdash; through short-form social media content designed to make stellar physics approachable for anyone curious about how old the stars really are.</p>

    <div class="proj-quote">
      <p class="proj-quote-text">"A good scientist is a good communicator, but it's a real treat to find a way to communicate our science to the public."</p>
      <p class="proj-quote-attribution">Mark Popinchalk, PhD &middot; Postdoctoral Scholar, AMNH</p>
    </div>

    <div class="proj-quote">
      <p class="proj-quote-text">"We are most excited about Mark's plans to use OpenSpace to reach new audiences via social media with accessible explanations of important science concepts."</p>
      <p class="proj-quote-attribution">Rosamond Kinzler, PhD &middot; OpenSpace PI, AMNH</p>
    </div>

  </div>
</div>
